title: Automatic processing of speech in cognitive disorders
summary: It is not always easy to detect problems with memory or thinking associated with neurological disorders. We do not yet have good tests that can detect very subtle changes.  In this study, we will use a speech test that automatically recognises very subtle changes in speech and language.  We now want to check whether the test works well.

interventions.name: Patients with a diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease or vascular cognitive impairment as well as healthy control subjects will be included. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of Alzheimer´s disease (AD), Parkinson’s disease (PD), vascular cognitive impairment (VCI) according to current national and international diagnostic criteria guidelines (S3 Demenz Leitlinien)
Exclusion criteria:
Inability to consent based on severity of cognitive impairment, as defined by a stage of moderate to severe dementia, defined by a Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) total score >=2, according to clinical records.  
For the healthy (neurotypical) control group: history of past or current neurological or major psychiatric disorder, severe traumatic brain injury, alcohol or drug abuse.
